definition.text: An area, usually in a city, where polluting vehicles are barred or charged for entering, to improve air quality.

facts.text: Many zones do not physically block entry but fine non-compliant vehicles unless a daily charge has been paid, often checked by number-plate cameras.
They work: diesel particulates fall in most zones and health improves, often because people replace polluting vehicles with cleaner ones.
People who need a car but cannot afford a cleaner one are hit hardest, so some cities enforce zones only where public transport exists or subsidise alternatives.
As of 2019 there were about 250 low-emission zones helping meet EU health-based air quality limits; London's, from 2008, was the world's largest.

title: Minimum energy performance standard

definition.text: A mandatory specification that caps how much energy an appliance or other device may use to do a given task.

facts.text: It usually requires a set test procedure, and may include non-energy requirements so that performance and user satisfaction do not suffer.
A refrigerator, for example, must hold set temperatures while using at most a specified amount of electricity, depending on its size and features.
California began appliance efficiency rules in 1978, and they became US national standards in 1988.
Standards are often paired with energy rating labels that help consumers choose products using less energy.
